notes: Actual receipts and disbursements for calendar year 2024, as the county reported them in its Annual Financial Report (cash basis). Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school corporations with their own taxes, so they are not included. The county collects property and local income taxes for every government in the county and pays them over; that money is left out.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
The county reported $27,684,523 of general fund spending without departments, so it cannot be split between services and overhead; the county is not scored on services or overhead.
Money the county holds for others or passes through (tax settlements, payroll and clearing accounts, trusts and escrow; $576,014,409 received) is left out.
Borrowing ($19,050,000) is not counted as revenue.
$4,383,604 of notes and bonds paid off with new borrowing (refinancing) is left out of debt service.
Distributions to other governments ($709,748) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: As of April 2024, the Hendricks County Sheriff's Office operates 12 Flock Safety automated license plate readers. The agency stores ALPR data for 30 days.

notes: Actual receipts and disbursements for calendar year 2024, as the town reported them in its Annual Financial Report (cash basis). Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school corporations with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Hendricks County and the township they live in.

Indiana's chart of accounts has no function codes, so spending is assigned to a service from the department or fund name (a police department or fire fund is public safety, a motor vehicle highway fund roads, a sewage utility fund utilities); spending in other funds with general names counts as general government.
The town reported $65,194 of general fund spending without departments, so it cannot be split between services and overhead; the town is not scored on services or overhead.
Money the town holds for others or passes through (tax settlements, payroll and clearing accounts, trusts and escrow; $106 received) is left out.
Transfers between funds, purchases of investments and payroll withholdings paid over are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is principal outstanding at year end on bonds, notes, leases and loans, as reported.
Political money is not scored: Indiana local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county election board, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
